standard.title: Unknown values in multiplication equations
standard.description: Find unknown values in numerical equations involving multiplication and division using the properties of numbers and operations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can find unknown values in equations involving addition and subtraction (AC9M4A02). They have not yet applied properties of multiplication and division (commutativity, associativity, equivalence) to find unknown values.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students find unknown values in numerical equations involving multiplication and division using properties of numbers and operations.
standard._audit_notes: SPLIT_REQUIRED: Node 2 — checkpoint bundles truth-value determination ('determine whether equations are true/false') with unknown-finding ('find unknown values'). Wider tier enriches only the unknown-finding move (two-sided equations, multi-operation equivalences). Each move warrants its own node with its own width.

nodes.label: Properties of multiplication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate that multiplication is commutative and associative, and that division is neither.
nodes.minimum_width: Show that a×b=b×a using materials or arrays; show a case where a÷b ≠ b÷a; explain the difference.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate commutativity and associativity of multiplication across multiple examples; explain why division is not commutative; connect to array representations.
wider: Investigate the distributive property: a×(b+c) = a×b + a×c
Use the properties to derive unknown facts from known ones
success_criteria: Student demonstrates commutativity with an example and explanation
Student correctly identifies that division is not commutative with an example

nodes.label: Equivalent number sentences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use equivalence and number properties to determine whether multiplication/division equations are true and to find unknown values.
nodes._node_audit: SPLIT_REQUIRED: Checkpoint pairs truth-value reasoning with unknown-finding. Wider tier (two-sided equations, unknowns on both sides) only enriches the unknown-finding move. Node should be split into: (2a) Evaluating equation truth-value using relational thinking; (2b) Finding unknown values using equivalence properties.
nodes.minimum_width: Determine whether a given multiplication/division equation is true or false; explain the reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply relational thinking to find unknown values in equations like 3×5=30÷□; use equivalence reasoning across a range of structures.
wider: Create equivalent number sentences using multiple operations
Use equations with unknowns in both sides: 4×□ = □×6

response_modes.reason: Relational thinking (understanding = as 'same value', not 'write the answer') requires an explicit scaffold. Students who have learned = as an answer prompt make systematic errors with balanced equations.

The variety of equation structures (unknown in different positions, multiple unknowns, cross-operation equivalence) exposes how relational thinking generalises. Breadth prevents students from learning the structure of one template.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Two-sided equations and multi-operation equivalences give advancing students genuine algebraic structure to work with.
nodes.hinge_reason: Relational understanding of = is the prerequisite for Node 3 — students who treat = as 'write the answer' cannot formulate or verify equations arising from practical contexts.
success_criteria: Student determines whether an equation is true/false with correct reasoning
Student finds an unknown value in a multiplication/division equation using properties

nodes.label: Finding unknowns in context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can find unknown values in numerical equations arising from practical contexts using multiplication and division properties.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a practical problem that requires finding an unknown value in a multiplication or division equation; show the equation and solution.
nodes.typical_width: Apply properties of multiplication and division to find unknowns in a range of practical and abstract contexts; connect equation-solving to word problem structures.
wider: Design word problems that require unknown-value equations to solve
Connect to scaling contexts: if 3 books cost $21, what does 1 cost? Equation: 3 × □ = 21

response_modes.reason: Applying equation reasoning in practical contexts requires properties knowledge, equation structure understanding and context interpretation to work together — the integrated application of the strand's learning.

success_criteria: Student writes an equation for a practical problem and finds the unknown value
Student verifies the solution by substituting back into the equation
